#86 arm B (540b0ec235) against arm A at master (a1691ae68e), two commits of
behaviour-bearing change apart plus a selftest and NOTES.

WHAT CHANGED BETWEEN THE ARMS. 7140d94731 replaces the unconditional silent
`while (glGetError() != GL_NO_ERROR) {}` at the top of
pgraph_gl_shader_load_from_memory() -- Android only -- with a helper that
drains exactly the same backlog and names each error on a logcat line tagged
[glerr], repeats counted rather than printed. a09ba73f2f adds
docs/testing/glerr_report_selftest.{c,sh}, which nothing in the emulator
builds or runs. Nothing else in the tree is touched.

THE ONLY LEG, AND IT IS AN INERTNESS LEG: better=0 and worse=0 over the
must_not_move set, i.e. every scored capture in those five suites is the same
distance from its golden in both arms. I predict this because the patch adds
no GL call, removes none, and reorders none: the set of errors drained on
entry is identical, the shader compiled is identical, and the only new work is
__android_log_print on a path that previously did nothing. The non-Android
path is byte-identical, so on any arm that is not Android this is not a change
at all.

NAMING THE WORLD IN WHICH IT FAILS, since an inert prediction that cannot fail
is not a prediction. Three concrete ones. (1) The helper stops draining --
if the loop were rewritten so that an error survives the call, the glGetError
eleven lines below reads it, treats the binary as failed, deletes the program
and returns false; the shader is then recompiled from source. That recompile
produces a working shader, so the SCORES may well not move -- which is exactly
why the selftest checks the drain directly rather than trusting this leg to
catch it. Stated so the leg is not credited with a check it does not perform.
(2) The helper is called somewhere other than shader load, or more than once
per load, which would show as timing-sensitive captures moving. (3) The
report's cost is not free: __android_log_print on every shader load of every
frame -- what the power-of-ten suppression exists to prevent -- would slow the
run enough to move captures whose content depends on how much work lands in a
frame. Leg 3 is the one this arm can actually catch, and it is a real risk of
this patch shape rather than a hypothetical.

WHAT A PASS DOES NOT LICENSE. A pass says the change moved no pixels. It says
nothing whatever about whether the report works: the [glerr] line is not in
the golden comparison and a device run on healthy code is expected to emit
none at all, which is indistinguishable at the pixel level from the silent
drain it replaces. The evidence that the report works is
docs/testing/glerr_report_selftest.sh (host compiler, both header sets, with a
pre-#86 falsification build that must fail by name), plus, on a device, a
deliberately provoked GL error before a shader load producing exactly one
line. NOTES.md states what a run's `grep '\[glerr\]'` should and should not
show.

WHAT NEITHER ARM CAN SHOW. Neither arm is a build by the shipping toolchain of
the code under test: the block is inside #ifdef __ANDROID__ and this lane has
no NDK. If arm B is built for Android by the dispatcher then the build itself
is the missing check, and its success is worth more than the pixel comparison
this file registers.

SUITE CHOICE. Five suites that exercise the GL shader path heavily and are
large enough that a real disturbance would be visible: Texture_render_target
(40 captures in the 2026-09-12 corpus), Blend_tests (105),
Texture_shadow_comparator (288), Texture_format (40), Window_clip (92).
2D_BorderTex_SZ and the rest of Texture_border are deliberately absent: that
capture's ten-run band on one unchanged APK is 0 0 0 0 0 146 181 1847 2352
2430 5640, so a single-run delta on it is a coin flip and would make a
must-not-move leg a lottery ticket.
